enquiry: We want to monitor water content in a clear ethanol-water stream in our solvent recovery unit. Water content is between 0.5 and 5 % w/w, the line runs at 25 °C in a DN50 stainless steel pipe, and the analyzer can sit in a control room about 20 m away. Our reference is Karl Fischer titration in the lab, and we need an updated value every minute.

clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today when water content is only known from lab Karl Fischer results, and which operating decision should the minute-by-minute value support?
clarification_questions.why: Defines the decision (e.g. control of recovery, product quality release) and therefore the required response and accuracy.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Decision unknown; the first step is to define the control or monitoring action with the client before choosing a method.

clarification_questions.question: What are the pressure, flow rate and any fouling, deposit or cleaning (CIP) conditions in the DN50 line?
clarification_questions.why: Determines probe type, mounting and whether the sensor must withstand cleaning or fouling.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Pressure, flow and fouling unknown; a fouling-tolerant, non-contact or easily cleaned arrangement is assumed to be needed until confirmed.

clarification_questions.question: Besides water, what other components are in the stream, and do they vary (other solvents, dissolved solids, bubbles, entrained gas, or temperature changes)?
clarification_questions.why: Other components can overlap the water signal and invalidate a calibration if the composition changes.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Composition beyond ethanol and water unknown; calibration validity across composition changes must be checked in lab screening.

clarification_questions.question: Where exactly on the DN50 pipe would the sensor be installed, and is there a free connection (nozzle, bypass or flow cell) and an existing fiber or cable route to the control room?
clarification_questions.why: The measuring point and the fiber route determine the probe geometry and whether the fiber can carry the required wavelengths over about 20 m.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Installation point and route unknown; a probe-to-analyzer link of about 20 m is assumed as stated, with fiber type to be determined.

clarification_questions.question: How is the Karl Fischer reference sample taken (sampling point, timing, sample volume) and what is its known accuracy or repeatability?
clarification_questions.why: Time-aligned reference samples and the reference accuracy set what the online sensor can be validated against.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference accuracy unknown; comparison with the Karl Fischer method requires time-aligned samples and a stated reference uncertainty.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy is required across the 0.5 to 5 % w/w range, and what response time is acceptable beyond the one-minute update?
clarification_questions.why: Accuracy and response time decide whether a few-wavelength sensor is enough or a broader method is needed.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Accuracy and response time unknown; the one-minute update is the only stated requirement.

clarification_questions.question: Is the solvent recovery area classified as hazardous (flammable ethanol vapour), and what installation constraints apply to the sensor and fibers?
clarification_questions.why: Hazardous area rules restrict the sensor and cabling, and therefore which optical setup is permissible.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Area classification unknown; the sensor location must be checked against site safety rules before any design.

clarification_questions.question: What is the budget range and the expected number of measuring points, and is a single online analyzer or a repeated installation intended?
clarification_questions.why: Budget and scale decide between a single robust sensor and a more complex system.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Budget and scale unknown; a single-point installation is assumed for the first assessment.

flags_before_revision.detail: not_supported: The cited S02 p.6 page lists transmission ranges for fibers, including PIR and chalcogenide fibers that transmit in the mid-IR (e.g. chalcogenide 1100-6500 nm, polycrystalline 3000 nm-17 um). The claim that silica fibers cannot carry mid-IR is partly supported by the chart showing silica ranges only to 2400 nm, but the statement that the materials give no link lengths for mid-IR fibers is accurate; the wording is acceptable only as a silica-range statement. Fix: Restrict the claim to: silica fibers on S02 p.6 cover only up to about 2400 nm, and S02 p.6 gives no link lengths for mid-IR fibers.

different_context: The S01 p.18 quote about NIR transmission being preferred applies to dairy milk products, not to general clear liquids or petroleum. Adding water -OH NIR band support from S01 p.10 does not establish water content in this context, and S01 p.10 only describes NIR overtones generally. Fix: State that S01 p.18 supports NIR transmission for transparent or semi-transparent dairy liquids such as skim milk, whey, or permeate, and cite S01 p.10 only for the general NIR overtone description.

not_supported: S02 p.13 shows ATR absorbance vs water content in oil with ZrO2 or diamond tips, and absorbance rises in the 3800-3000 cm-1 region. It does not state that the measurement is MIR-ATR for a specific liquid beyond the oil example, and the claim's quoted label is accurate but the stated technique extends the page. Fix: Describe the slide as showing ATR absorbance spectra of oil with 0.1% to 2.0% water in the 4000-2000 cm-1 range, citing S02 p.13 only.

overstated: The claim asserts that a 20 m link needs mid-IR fibers, but S02 p.6 and S04 p.1 do not state link requirements for a 20 m path; S04 p.1 only mentions fiber-probe use in general. Fix: Say that the materials do not give a link length for mid-IR fibers and that a 20 m link is unconfirmed by the cited pages.

not_supported: The cited table rows list 1-10 mm for transmission or transflection probes on liquids, and S01 p.18 supports the transmission path control, but the table entries cover many methods and the claim selects a probe for a clear liquid without saying which row applies. Fix: Cite only TABLE:r7 (NIR transmission or transflection probe, liquid, 1-10 mm) and S01 p.18 for the path-length guidance.

not_supported: The cited pages do not contain a rule check with spectral coverage labels such as Vis-NIR silica partial or PIR partial for NIR and MIR; S02 p.6 gives ranges but the partial/no coverage judgments are not stated there. Fix: Report the ranges directly from S02 p.6: Vis-NIR silica 350-2400 nm and polycrystalline IR 3000 nm-17 um, without the partial or no coverage labels.

overstated: S01 p.10 describes NIR overlapping bands requiring chemometrics but does not state that other solvents or impurities invalidate a matrix-specific calibration; that conclusion is stronger than the page. Fix: Say that overlapping NIR bands suggest chemometrics are needed, so other components in the stream may affect the model, citing S01 p.10.

not_supported: S02 p.6 gives transmission ranges for fiber families but does not state that the 20 m link is undefined; the claim about undefined fiber family is an inference not stated on the page. Fix: State only that S02 p.6 gives spectral ranges for fiber families and no link lengths for mid-IR fibers.

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [guidance]

fiber_limits_wavelength: The fiber determines which wavelengths reach the probe. Silica fibers transmit up to about 2.4 um and cannot carry mid-IR; mid-IR needs chalcogenide, polycrystalline or hollow-waveguide fibers. [S02 p.6; S04 p.1]
remote_measurement_nir_silica: NIR works with standard glass optics and silica fibers, which suits remote online measurement; robust silica cables of 100-300 m exist. [S01 p.5; S02 p.7]

geometry_follows_optics: Clear liquids suit transmission or transflection; opaque, concentrated or powder samples suit diffuse reflection; highly absorbing or 'black' liquids suit ATR. [S01 Table 1 (p.6); S01 p.16; S01 p.17-18]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [guidance]
